profile.headline: Engineer, Software Developer, Apple.com
profile.summary:
As a graduate from Cal Poly's Graphic Communication major, I have focused my development skills towards a career that allows me to demonstrate my expertise in web-accessibility and my passion for web-usability.

Before graduating in December 2008, my job as a Web Content Developer for the Cal Poly Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL) gave me the unique opportunity to design a web site fully compliant with Section 508 requirements for web-accessibility--a federal standard which ensures websites are easily navigable by visually-impaired users.

Since then, I've worked as a Web/Print design contractor for Fleet Management Solutions--rebuilding their corporate website for aggressive Search Engine Optimization (SEO) and improved usability.

On the side, I've built a successful freelance graphic/web design business, with projects such as professional portfolios, business-to-business sites, and content management system (CMS)-based e-commerce sites.

For two years, I worked at a digital agency called Level Studios, a Rosetta Company. I started out at Level as an Associate Interactive Developer, and progressed to a Senior Associate position.

Currently, I am employed at Apple in the Interactive Infrastructure department.

Specialties: Web Site Production, HTML5, CSS3, Web-Accessibility, Web-Usability, Interface Design, Search Engine Optimization, Content Managment, Marketing, Photoshop, Illustrator, Flash, Multimedia, Branding, Logo Design

positions.title: Senior Associate Interactive Developer
positions.description: As an interactive developer, I was responsible for collaborating with a team of project managers, graphic designers, engineers, and user experience experts to produce a variety of corporate websites and web applications. Specifically, I hand-coded HTML5 and CSS3 to build out web pages based on Photoshop design compositions and performed maintenance and updates to existing pages.

positions.title: Graphic / Web Design Contractor
positions.description:
In 2008, I spear-headed a complete rebuild of Fleet's corporate website with content and interface updates for usability and more agressive search engine optimization (SEO). Specifically, I switched the design from tabular to CSS-based layout using semantic markup to enhance usability, reduce file sizes, and improve efficiency of maintenance.

As part of a challenge to streamline the process for the FMS sales team, I improved the integration of web forms into the Salesforce.com lead management system.

Recently, I've had the opportunity to build my skills in JavaScript, creating a Return on Investment calculator for potential FMS customers.

Apart from my work on the FMS website, I've re-designed most of FMS's printed materials--including case studies, product data sheets, and brochures--with the purpose of promoting a consistent identity scheme.

positions.title: Freelance Graphic / Web Designer
positions.description:
Recently, my freelance business has been geared mostly towards web-design/development, with projects including professional portfolios, business-to-business sites, and CMS-based e-commerce sites. These challenges have given me the opportunity to enhance my skills in CSS, XHTML, PHP, Flash, and JavaScript.

In addition to my freelance web design, I've worked on a broad range designs for print. Most notably, I collaborated with Cal Poly's Special Collections to create post cards, posters, and panels for two exhibits featured at the Cal Poly Library. I've designed the identity scheme for several local business, including letterheads, business cards, envelopes, and product brochures. Additionally, I've performed complex photo manipulation for architectural & civic planning projects.

positions.title: Web Content Developer
positions.description:
My primary responsibility was to design and maintain the CTL's website, ensuring section 508 compliance for web accessibility, while adhering to Cal Poly's strict requirements for associate web sites. As part of this, I was  tasked with creating a new identity scheme for the CTL which carried through to all of its printed materials and PowerPoint presentations.

Most notable of my print design projects for the CTL was the quarterly 8-page newsletter sent out to all Cal Poly faculty. Each quarter, I collected articles from several faculty and staff members, performed basic copy editing, and then formatted everything in Adobe InDesign. Other print projects included learning posters and flyers. 

Because of Cal Poly's strict requirements for accessibility, I had the opportunity to master a variety of accessibility-related tools. I used Adobe Acrobat's Optical Character Recognition (OCR), PDF-tagging, and reading-order features to create accessible PDF documents. Adobe Captivate enabled me to develop interactive step-by-step software tutorials for faculty, with voice-overs and closed captioning for disabled users. For video projects, I added captions using the National Center for Accessible Media (NCAM)'s Media Access Generator (MAGpie).

company.name: Cal Poly Center for Teaching and Learning (CTL)

positions.title: Web Offset Head Pressman (HP)
positions.description:
As a Head Pressman at UGS, I trained new students to setup, run, and maintain a Goss web offset newspaper printing press, and print Cal Poly's student-run newspaper, the "Mustang Daily," several times a week.

Apart from directing a team of trainees, I had the responsibility of minimizing ink/substrate waste, and contributing towards the continuous improvement of the press room procedures.
